correctness.rationale: For each positive integer abundance profile, the three Hill indices reduce exactly to the length, inverse squared-abundance sum, and inverse largest abundance. Discrete smoothing proves the minimum square sum with fixed length and maximum, and greedy majorization proves the maximum over longer bounded-part profiles. The exact exhaustive parameter scan for totals 1–14 has one surviving envelope at \((14,5,6,6,52,54)\). Square-sum parity and uniqueness of strict convexity extrema give exactly one witness. An independent pairwise enumeration of 20,283 unordered partition pairs and a distinct multiplicity-based partition generator reproduced the classification; all checks replayed from the delivered code path.

originality.rationale: The precise same-total-integer-census minimum for the concordant richness / inverse-dominance endpoints and opposing Hill–Simpson order, including uniqueness at the minimum, was not established by the inspected foundational, ecological-index-comparison, or indexed mathematical sources. Hill introduced the diversity scale, Patil–Taillie developed a diversity-order crossing framework, Morris et al. compared the named indices, and Roswell et al. explicitly discussed profile crossings. Those general statements do not logically imply the least integer total of 14 or the unique abundance-partition pair. The accessible full-text references and actual narrow/equivalent/broader searches found no directly dominating result, but uninspected Patil–Taillie and Hill full texts remain bibliographic risks. This is a best-knowledge comparison, not certified absence.
residual_risks: The Patil–Taillie 1982 crossing-point theorem was not obtainable in full. It could contain an overlooked special exact finite-census implication or example.
Only the Hill 1973 abstract/metadata could be inspected in full; no claim is made that its inaccessible primary body is non-covering.
Independent bibliographic verification is absent; an unindexed integer-partition or inequality source may already include this particular cutoff.

value.rationale: The least equal-community census at which intermediate Hill–Simpson diversity overturns concordant richness and reciprocal-dominance rankings is an intrinsic, motivated natural finite invariant of three ecologically standard summary measures. The classification is complete at the sharp boundary, and the balancing versus capped-concentration envelopes expose its structural cause. The result identifies exactly how small communities first display a nonmonotone relative diversity ranking along the standard three-anchor Hill scale. It neither claims general profile-order minimality nor treats computational reproducibility as its sole value.
